# Jubilab

> Jubilab helps you streamline biological sample to data with AI enablement: order sequencing from outside labs once, see every step, and get results with your own sample names, so scientists and AI agents can order, track and read results across dry labs, wet labs and logistics. It is for biotech teams, research groups and startups that send samples to outside labs, and for the labs that run their samples. We start with non-clinical genetics sequencing. Early access is by invitation: request access and we invite small groups first.

## What Jubilab does

- Order once: describe your samples and the sequencing service you need one time; Jubilab turns the request into a structured order that adapts to each supported provider.
- Follow every step: see when an order is accepted, when samples arrive, whether they pass QC, when the run starts and when results are ready.
- Get clean results back: a structured result manifest links output files to your own sample names and includes QC information; a failed sample is reported as failed, not as missing.
- Today an order moves between two sides that are managed separately and joined only by email and Excel: the dry lab side (scientists, researchers and the people who consume results) and the wet lab side (lab staff and logistics). Jubilab connects them with one order, one place to follow it and one clean result.
- For teams, every external lab in one workflow: one order structure instead of a different spreadsheet for every provider; clearer status as receipt, QC, run and delivery are reported, without repeatedly emailing a project manager; results tied to your own sample identifiers, with QC information and file checks. You keep the tools you already use.
- For labs and core facilities, three ways to connect, and a lab can stop at any step: (1) existing order emails and courier updates, with facts read from email labelled as such; (2) a simple status page with four buttons (received, QC done, run started, results ready) and result upload; (3) lab software through webhooks, and run progress from instruments. Jubilab connects to your existing tools and does not replace them.
- For AI agents and developers: structured orders, machine-readable status and structured results through API and MCP access for compatible clients.

## The value for your team

- Hours saved per week: email tracking, status updates, spreadsheets and not knowing where a sample is add up to hours of admin every week, and Jubilab takes that work off your team.
- Zero custom-built solutions to maintain: one connected layer handles the different structures, formats and communication between dry lab requirements, couriers, wet lab status updates and raw sample data.
- Ready to streamline dry lab to wet lab with AI: built for AI agent workflows that take a hypothesis all the way to wet lab sample processing.

## Guides

- [Guides](https://jubilab.io/guides/): practical how-tos for bioinformatics teams, written to be useful without Jubilab, each with tested commands, sources and a review date, from our earlier work on data provenance
- [How to check which reference genome build a VCF or BAM used](https://jubilab.io/guides/reference-genome-build-vcf-bam/): read VCF and BAM headers with bcftools and samtools, compare contig lengths and test REF alleles
- [What parameters produced this result?](https://jubilab.io/guides/what-parameters-produced-this-result/): finding the parameters of a Nextflow, Snakemake or shell run, what gets lost, and what a good record contains
- [Nextflow provenance and lineage: what each tool records](https://jubilab.io/guides/nextflow-provenance-and-lineage-compared/): what Nextflow's log, trace, report and experimental lineage feature record, compared with Snakemake

## Blog

- [Blog](https://jubilab.io/blog/): notes on data provenance, lineage and reproducibility in bioinformatics from our earlier work, each with sources and open questions. Jubilab is a way to order lab work once and follow it to results
- [AI agents in the lab need a record, not a chat history](https://jubilab.io/blog/ai-agents-need-a-record-not-just-chat-history/): Agents can run analyses, but a chat transcript is not a record of how a result was made. Our view on what a record for lab agents holds.
- [Conda for genomics: export, history or lock file?](https://jubilab.io/blog/conda-environments-genomics-export-history-lock/): Three ways to save a conda environment, what each keeps in a small test, and what we still wonder about for genomics.
- [How to compare two pipeline runs](https://jubilab.io/blog/how-to-compare-two-pipeline-runs/): What counts as a difference between two runs, a manual way to diff them, and what lineage diff and nf-diff showed on a toy pair.
- [Inherited a pipeline? A first-week checklist](https://jubilab.io/blog/inherited-pipeline-first-week-checklist/): A practical checklist for rebuilding how results were made when you inherit someone else's analysis, and what to record as you go.
- [Lifting a VCF over: what to record](https://jubilab.io/blog/lifting-a-vcf-over-what-to-record/): Liftover moves variants between assemblies and can lose some. What to record so you can explain the differences later.
- [Local-first for lab data: what stays on your machine](https://jubilab.io/blog/local-first-for-lab-data/): Local-first ideas applied to lab records: what stays on your machine, where the cloud helps, and how our earlier work used them.
- [Pin your containers by digest, not by tag](https://jubilab.io/blog/pin-your-containers-by-digest-not-by-tag/): A tag is a label that can move; a digest names one image. How to find, use and write down the digest a pipeline ran with.
- [When should a pipeline get a new version number?](https://jubilab.io/blog/pipeline-version-numbers-two-conventions/): Two published pipeline versioning conventions side by side, where they differ, and why we treat it as an open question.
- [Provenance vs lineage in bioinformatics: examples](https://jubilab.io/blog/provenance-vs-lineage-in-bioinformatics/): Two overlapping words, one toy variant calling pipeline, and the questions each one helps you answer about a VCF.
- [RO-Crate, BioCompute Objects and PROV: which one?](https://jubilab.io/blog/ro-crate-biocompute-objects-and-prov/): PROV, RO-Crate and BioCompute Objects in plain words, what nf-prov writes, and how to choose. Jubilab supports none of them.
- [Same FASTQs, different variants: where it creeps in](https://jubilab.io/blog/same-fastqs-different-variants/): Same FASTQs, different VCFs? What published studies report, how to isolate the stage, and what to record to explain it.
- [Sample swaps: the tools, and what a run record can say](https://jubilab.io/blog/sample-swaps-tools-and-what-a-run-record-says/): How swaps are found, per three papers, and what a run record can and cannot tell you once one is suspected.
- [Samplesheet traps that quietly change your run](https://jubilab.io/blog/samplesheet-traps-that-change-your-run/): A samplesheet is an input like any other. Five ways a small CSV goes wrong, and what to keep with the run.
- [Ten simple rules for reproducible research, revisited](https://jubilab.io/blog/ten-simple-rules-reproducible-research-revisited/): Ten rules from a 2013 paper, read against today's workflow tools: which ones tools help with, and which are still open.
- [What a core should hand over with every project](https://jubilab.io/blog/what-a-core-should-hand-over-with-every-project/): A checklist of what a sequencing or analysis core could send beyond the data files, and why it helps clients and staff.
- [What is data provenance in bioinformatics?](https://jubilab.io/blog/what-is-data-provenance-in-bioinformatics/): Provenance is the record of how a result was made. What it holds, what tools keep today, and what we still wonder about.
- [Where did my intermediate files go?](https://jubilab.io/blog/where-did-my-intermediate-files-go/): Work directories get cleaned or purged. What that does to resume, what to keep, and what a record can still say afterwards.
- [Which annotation versions produced this VCF?](https://jubilab.io/blog/which-annotation-versions-produced-this-vcf/): An annotated VCF may not name its VEP cache, ClinVar or gnomAD release. What the docs say, how to check, what to write down.
- [Why a record should say what it doesn't know](https://jubilab.io/blog/why-a-record-should-say-what-it-doesnt-know/): A tidy record with silently guessed fields can mislead. Four evidence statuses, a worked example and a spreadsheet version.
- [Why did my task run again? Nextflow and Snakemake](https://jubilab.io/blog/why-did-my-task-run-again-nextflow-snakemake/): What Nextflow and Snakemake compare before skipping a task, how to see why one reran, and what a rerun means for history.
- [Write the methods paragraph from your run record](https://jubilab.io/blog/write-methods-paragraph-from-run-record/): A fill-in methods paragraph for pipeline analyses, and where each value comes from when you read it off a record.
